questions.question: Riding gloves are usually made of what?
questions.explanation: Motorcycle riding gloves are usually made of leather. They improve your grip and protect your hands and fingers.

questions.question: Which item is NOT protective clothing for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Safe motorcycle riders wear a helmet, eye protection, a jacket, long pants, sturdy boots, and gloves. Sandals do not protect your feet.

questions.question: How does a motorcycle's brake light compare to a car's brake light?
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's brake light is usually not as noticeable as a car's brake light. Flashing your brake light before you slow down or stop helps other drivers see what you are doing.

questions.question: Which of these does NOT need to be checked before riding?
questions.explanation: Before every ride, check your tires, controls, chain, sprockets, shock absorbers, bolts and screws, and brakes. A small problem can be very dangerous on a motorcycle.

questions.question: What is the best way to handle a tailgater?

options.text: Change lanes and let them pass
Use your horn and make rude gestures
Speed up to create more distance

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass
questions.explanation: Change lanes and let the tailgater pass when you can. Speeding up may cause them to tailgate you even faster, which increases danger.

questions.question: What is the correct body position on a motorcycle?

options.text: Sit forward enough so your arms are slightly bent when holding the grips
Sit as far back as possible and stretch to reach the grips
Lean forward so your arms support your weight
Keep your knees far from the gas tank

questions.correctAnswerText: Sit forward enough so your arms are slightly bent when holding the grips
questions.explanation: Sit forward so your arms are slightly bent when holding the grips. This position lets you easily reach and use the controls.

questions.question: What should you do with mirror checks?

options.text: Make them part of your normal routine
Avoid them because they distract you
Avoid them because other drivers can see you
Only do them in bad weather

questions.correctAnswerText: Make them part of your normal routine
questions.explanation: You need to know what is behind you. Check your mirrors often as part of your normal routine.

questions.question: Because alcohol does not need to be digested, what happens?

options.text: It reaches your brain within minutes
It takes a long time to feel its effects
Your body removes it very quickly

questions.correctAnswerText: It reaches your brain within minutes
questions.explanation: Alcohol enters your bloodstream quickly and reaches your brain within minutes because it does not need to be digested. Your body removes about one drink per hour.

questions.question: What is often found in the center of a lane?
questions.explanation: Oil and grease from cars form a strip in the center of each lane. When roads are dry, it is usually still safe for a motorcycle to ride on this center strip.

questions.question: Which surface is slippery and hard to control?
questions.explanation: Wet pavement, loose gravel or sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lane markings, and metal covers can all be slippery. Ride with extra care on these surfaces.

questions.question: When does alcohol impairment begin?

options.text: At about half the legal limit.

questions.explanation: Even one drink can affect your ability to ride safely. You can be impaired before reaching the legal blood alcohol limit. Never drink and ride.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: What is a simple way to make your motorcycle easier to see?

options.text: Ride with a large flag attached to the frame.
Ride on the shoulder whenever possible.

questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at all times. Wear bright, reflective clothing. Use your turn signals and brake light properly to stay visible.

questions.question: What is the best gear to wear while riding?
questions.explanation: Wear gear for protection. Use a DOT-approved helmet, eye or face protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: When should you use a turn signal?

options.text: When you plan to speed up.

questions.explanation: Use your turn signal every time you turn or change lanes, even if you think no one is watching.

questions.question: What does a DOT-approved helmet do?

options.text: Makes it harder to control your motorcycle.

questions.explanation: A helmet protects your head and neck in a crash. It greatly improves your chances of avoiding serious injury. A DOT-approved helmet does not block your side vision.

questions.question: How many brakes do most motorcycles have?

options.text: Three brakes: front, rear, and emergency.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have two brakes—one for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel.

questions.question: What should you do when riding on bridge grating?

options.text: Stay on the far right side of the lane.
Stay on the far left side of the lane.
Relax, maintain steady speed, and ride straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, maintain steady speed, and ride straight.
questions.explanation: Bridge grating may cause your motorcycle to weave slightly. This is normal and not dangerous. Stay relaxed and keep a steady speed. Do not zigzag to fight the movement.

questions.question: What should you do before riding an unfamiliar motorcycle?

options.text: Ride it like you would your own bike since all bikes are the same.
Check the controls and shift pattern.
Trust the owner that everything works.
Assume you know where all the controls are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the controls and shift pattern.
questions.explanation: Each motorcycle is different. Check the controls and learn the gear pattern before riding. Test the throttle, clutch, and brakes before you start.

questions.question: In West Virginia, what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is considered legally intoxicated?
questions.explanation: In West Virginia, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher is legally intoxicated. Driving under the influence of alcohol is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: How do you control the accelerator on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: On a motorcycle, the accelerator is at the right handgrip. You control it with your right hand.

questions.question: A rectangular sign shows:
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs are rectangular with white background and black lettering. Rectangular signs show road rules that you must follow.

questions.question: When riding an unfamiliar motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Check if the seat is comfortable
Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding
Ride normally since all bikes are the same

questions.correctAnswerText: Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes before riding
questions.explanation: Every motorcycle is different. Before you ride, get to know the bike. Practice the throttle, clutch, and brakes several times to learn how they work.

questions.question: What brakes do most motorcycles have?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycles have one brake for the front wheel and one for the rear wheel. The front brake is stronger than the rear brake.

questions.question: To stop quickly, what should you do?

options.text: Press both brakes at the same time
Squeeze the front brake until it locks

questions.correctAnswerText: Press both brakes at the same time
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, use both brakes together. Do not grab or squeeze the front brake too hard. Never lock the brakes.
